en.headline: Wall Street Journal publisher convicted of deterring reporter from union role
en.dek: Eastern Magistrates’ Courts found Dow Jones guilty of preventing Selina Cheng from standing for Hong Kong Journalists Association chairmanship but cleared it of unlawful dismissal over the union activity.
body: A Hong Kong court on Thursday convicted the publisher of The Wall Street Journal of wilfully deterring a former reporter from exercising her right to take up a leadership role in a local press union.

Principal Magistrate David Cheung ruled that Dow Jones Publishing Co. (Asia) had required Selina Cheng to seek prior approval before running for chair of the Hong Kong Journalists Association in 2024, an arrangement he described as a wrongful application of the company’s code of conduct. The company was acquitted of a second charge that it had dismissed Cheng because of her union activities, the magistrate finding that a genuine restructuring could not be ruled out beyond reasonable doubt.

Cheng, who remains chair of the association, had launched a private prosecution after losing her job in July 2024. The maximum fine for the offence is HK$100,000. Sentencing is expected early next year.

zh.headline: 華爾街日報出版商阻記者競逐記協主席 被裁定有罪
zh.dek: 東區裁判法院裁定道瓊斯出版公司故意阻止前記者鄭嘉如行使工會權利，但裁定解僱指控不成立。
body: 東區裁判法院周四裁定《華爾街日報》出版商道瓊斯出版（亞洲）公司，故意阻止前記者鄭嘉如行使參與工會的權利，罪名成立。
主任裁判官張子惠指，公司要求鄭嘉如在2024年競逐香港記者協會主席前須先獲批准，屬錯誤及不合理地套用行為守則。至於指公司因她行使工會權利而解僱的第二項控罪，裁判官認為不能排除屬真正架構重組的可能性，裁定罪名不成立。
鄭嘉如在2024年7月失去工作後提出私人檢控，現仍擔任記協主席。該罪最高罰款10萬元，判刑預計明年初。
